title: [CQ-F03] Structured execution contract
description:
Objective: Extend existing task and submit_plan contract with intended behavior, criteria, invariants, compatibility, approved scope, reuse/source assumptions and check references.

Deliverable: Structured execution contract. This is task F03 of the approved full CQ rollout; consume this contract, not the whole reference document.

Scope boundaries: implement this behavior and its regression tests only. Later activation, other platform/client consumers and other task behaviors remain out of scope unless named here. Approved full CQ-01–CQ-08 rollout from the interactive implementation plan (2026-10-24). CQ-01 is already landed. Use original Moe source; daemon owns state, wrappers own host Git writes. User selected Moe-provisioned LOCAL Linux VMs (not cloud CI), coding/QA and checks isolated, and exact designated LOCAL BRANCH delivery. Strong profile stays disabled until isolation, evidence and client gates pass. Preserve legacy behavior and existing dirty bytes. Never directly edit .moe. No second revision authority, scheduler, graph database or native memory database.

Verification command (fresh, exit0 required): cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test

Dependency aliases (wired by Moe task ids after import): F02, M01.
definitionOfDone: Material changes advance planRevision through the same durable task write.
Sanitization, bounds and producer/consumer schema tests prevent silent contract loss.
Fresh verification `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` exits0 and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description:
Schema contract (packages/moe-daemon/src/types/schema.ts - CRLF working copy: edit with the Edit tool only, never Serena/sed, keep CRLF). No behavior change; `npx tsc --noEmit` from packages/moe-daemon stays clean.
(1) Add `export interface TaskExecutionContract` (just above `interface Task`) with exactly these eight optional keys, in this order: `intendedBehavior?: string` (observable behavior/outcome the change must produce); `acceptanceCriteria?: string[]` (behavior-level criteria; definitionOfDone stays the human-owned list); `invariants?: string[]`; `compatibility?: string[]` (legacy data, wire/protocol shapes and callers that must keep working); `approvedScope?: string[]` (symbols, interfaces and producer->consumer surfaces the change may touch - FILE scope stays each step's affectedFiles/newFiles, there is no second file list); `reuse?: string[]` (existing implementations reused, or why a new one is introduced); `sourceAssumptions?: string[]` (source facts the plan relies on, with path/symbol references); `checkRefs?: string[]` (required verification, each exactly as it will be run). JSDoc: optional per task (a docs fix may carry only intendedBehavior, an API change also compatibility); written only through validateExecutionContract (step 2), so a stored contract is canonical; every field is approval-relevant, so any change advances planRevision in the same write; it is never approval, readiness or evidence by itself.
(2) Add `executionContract?: TaskExecutionContract;` to `interface Task` right after `executionPolicySnapshot`. JSDoc: absent means no contract (legacy rows load unchanged: no migration, no schemaVersion bump); null or an empty contract clears it; test absence with `=== undefined`, never hasOwnProperty/`in` (after a clear the in-memory row holds an own undefined key that a reload does not have).
(3) Rewrite the `Task.planRevision` JSDoc per the F02 QA handoff (task comment comment-6108bfafc96b461b8ee8031f7bb4339a): the material surface is the canonical approval projection - ordered step ids, original and effective (active-amendment) instructions, affectedFiles/newFiles - plus definitionOfDone and executionContract. Execution status, startedAt/completedAt, reported modifiedFiles, progress notes, amendment audit fields and inactive amendment history are NOT material; reopen neither resets it nor advances it by clearing execution evidence. Keep the existing domain, caller-stamp stripping and legacy-absent-is-0 sentences.

Consumer: get_context serves the contract to every role (packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/getContext.ts - LF; extend executionContract.test.ts).
- In the task payload right after `taskRails` add `...(task.executionContract !== undefined && task.executionContract !== null ? { executionContract: task.executionContract } : {})`, commented: mandatory execution context for workers and QA, so never role-trimmed (not in ROLE_OMITTED, not behind trimForQa); omitted (not null) when absent so a legacy task's payload stays byte-identical. Do not add it to view 'status' (contextStatus). Mention 'executionContract when set' in the tool description's task list.
Consumer tests (describe 'get_context execution contract'), reusing step 4's submit fixture: call getContextTool for workerId 'worker-1', 'qa-1' and 'architect-1' (default views; the role resolves from the id prefix) and for 'qa-1' with view 'full' -> each task.executionContract toStrictEqual the stored canonical contract and no `omitted` array names it; the same after reloading state from disk; for a legacy task no role's task payload has an executionContract property.

Docs (docs/SCHEMA.md, docs/MCP_SERVER.md - both LF). Re-read the landed code before writing each claim; keep claims exact.
SCHEMA.md: (1) the Task listing near planRevision gets `executionContract?: TaskExecutionContract;` with a one-line comment; (2) a new `### executionContract` subsection after `### executionPolicySnapshot`: the eight fields and their meanings, bounds, canonical form, optional/legacy rule (absent = none, no migration), validation (refused with INVALID_INPUT, never truncated, unknown keys refused, null/empty clears), materiality (any change +1 in the same write; an equal contract, even with reordered keys, does not bump), writers (submit_plan replaces it; every updateTask writer is validated), file scope stays in steps, get_context serves it to every role; (3) correct the stale `### planRevision` bullets - the 'Every retained key inside a step participates' bullet and the reopen bullet still describe pre-F02 behavior - to the canonical projection plus the contract (F02 QA handoff comment-6108bfafc96b461b8ee8031f7bb4339a); (4) Validation Rules > Task: add the contract bounds.
MCP_SERVER.md: the submit_plan Parameters block gets `executionContract?: { ... }`; a Notes bullet covering validation (INVALID_INPUT with context.field, no truncation), the forbidden-pattern scan of contract text (required patterns still come from steps), replace semantics and the same-write planRevision bump; the get_context section notes `task.executionContract` (present when set, every role, never trimmed).

Verification - the gate, run once after steps 1-6: `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` (exit 0; its fresh output tail is the complete_task evidence) plus `npx tsc --noEmit` (exit 0) and the test-file typecheck `npx tsc --noEmit --ignoreConfig --target ES2022 --module ESNext --moduleResolution bundler --strict --esModuleInterop --skipLibCheck --resolveJsonModule src/state/executionContract.test.ts` (tsconfig excludes tests).
WSL environment: the shared checkout's node_modules are Windows-native (vitest: 'Cannot find native binding'); never npm install there. Run in a native-Linux snapshot: `SNAP=$(mktemp -d /tmp/moe-f03-gate.XXXXXX); git archive HEAD packages/moe-daemon scripts docs CLAUDE.md .gitignore package.json | tar -x -C $SNAP`, copy ONLY this task's eight files over it (cmp each against the worktree), `ln -s /tmp/moe-linux-daemon.3EJTl5/repo/packages/moe-daemon/node_modules $SNAP/packages/moe-daemon/node_modules` (symlink the directory itself; if it is gone, npm ci in a separate scratch copy with an unchanged lockfile), unset every MOE_* variable, use a Linux-only PATH, run from $SNAP/packages/moe-daemon, and report the exact command and environment in complete_task.
Must pass UNCHANGED: approvalRevision.acceptance.test.ts (the F05 group stays skipped), submitPlan.test.ts, getContext.test.ts and WebSocketServer.test.ts. A failure there is a compatibility break in production code: fix the code, never those tests. For a failure in a file this task did not touch, rerun it alone on HEAD's plain archive to prove it pre-exists before calling it foreign.

Adversarial self-review with mutation proof (load adversarial-self-review). Read the whole diff as an attacker: concurrent submit_plan + UPDATE_TASK on one task (both under the state mutex; still one bump per write); null/empty/huge/Unicode/NUL contracts; a board echo of the whole task (equal contract -> no bump); a hand-edited corrupt stored contract (unrelated writes and get_context never throw); own undefined key after a clear (every read uses === undefined); no forbidden-pattern token in any source; CRLF kept in schema.ts/taskStore.ts/validators.ts (git diff --stat shows no whole-file churn).
Mutation proof (pattern-mutation-union-proves-every-test): in a scratch copy of the snapshot, never the shared checkout, apply these together, then individually for any you doubt: drop `!contractChanged` from the early return; set truncate:true for items; skip rejectUnknownFields; delete the updateTask validation line; omit the key from updatePayload; always send null from submit_plan; drop the forbidden-only contract rails scan; fold contract text into the step rails text; remove the get_context projection; gate the projection behind !trimForQa. Each must turn at least one named test red; add a test for any survivor. If any byte changed, rerun step 7's command and submit THAT output. comments.author: architect-6e3edf85
comments.content:
Architect note on the 8-file plan-size warning (planRevision 1). The plan edits exactly these files, each needed:
- schema.ts: type and doc
- validators.ts: strict validator
- taskStore.ts: every-writer validation and planRevision materiality
- submitPlan.ts: producer
- getContext.ts: consumer
- the new src/state/executionContract.test.ts
- docs/SCHEMA.md and docs/MCP_SERVER.md

It stays one coherent change: the contract must be persisted and served together for DoD 3's producer/consumer tests. The docs also fix the stale planRevision prose that F02 QA handed off in comment-6108bfaf.

Defaults I chose under TURBO, for reviewers:
1. The contract is one optional Task.executionContract with eight fields. intendedBehavior is a string; acceptanceCriteria, invariants, compatibility, approvedScope, reuse, sourceAssumptions and checkRefs are string lists.
2. File scope stays in the steps' affectedFiles/newFiles. approvedScope names symbols and producer/consumer surfaces only.
3. Malformed or over-bound input is refused with INVALID_INPUT, never truncated. Unknown keys are refused. null or an empty contract clears it.
4. Any contract change advances planRevision once, in the same write.
5. A submit_plan resubmission replaces the contract: omitting it clears a stored one.
6. Contract text is scanned for forbidden patterns only. Required patterns must still appear in the steps.
7. get_context serves the contract to every role and omits it when absent.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Decisions taken with defaults (TURBO; recorded here and in a task comment):
1. One optional Task.executionContract object with eight flat fields (intendedBehavior string + seven string lists). Rejected: a separate contract store or contract revision counter (epic rail: one approval revision authority, no parallel stores); nesting into ImplementationStep or DoD strings (loses structure; DoD stays human-owned).
2. No file list inside the contract: file scope stays the steps' affectedFiles/newFiles, which F02 already treats as approved scope. approvedScope names symbols/interfaces/producer->consumer surfaces. Avoids two disagreeing sources of file scope.
3. Strict validation at every writer (submit_plan and taskStore.updateTask), sharing one set of bounds; never a slicing sanitizer. Slicing is the 5000/10000 step-description truncation bug class that DoD item 3 forbids.
4. Contract text gets a forbidden-pattern scan only. Folding it into the required-pattern check would weaken the steps' required-pattern rail; skipping the scan would let a forbidden token ride in approval text (same reasoning that put newFiles into the rail text).
5. Replace semantics on resubmission: a contract describes the plan it was submitted with, so an omitted contract clears a stored one (key sent only when there is something to set or clear, keeping legacy payloads byte-identical).
6. get_context projects the stored value raw, consistent with implementationPlan; stored contracts are canonical by construction. A compact packet/role-trim redesign is CQ-C01's job.
7. Kept as ONE task despite 8 distinct files (warn >5, hard cap 10): producer, store, consumer and docs must change together for the contract to be persisted AND served, and the docs fix was explicitly requested by F02 QA. Splitting would add a dependency hop in front of F04-F12.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: taskStore.updateTask is the single chokepoint for every task writer (submit_plan, amend_plan_step, reopen, request_replan, plugin UPDATE_TASK); order is sanitize -> guards -> derivePlanRevision -> writeEntity -> map.set -> activity -> emit. derivePlanRevision bumps once per write via sameSanitizedSurface (structural; array order significant, key order not). validators.ts has two families: validate* throws before disk, sanitize* never throws; reuse requirePlainObject, rejectUnknownFields and validateStringValue (truncate:false, allowNewlines:true). validateStringArrayValue truncates and forbids newlines, so do not reuse it. get_context's task payload is projected field by field (a new Task field is invisible until projected); ROLE_OMITTED/trimForQa trim QA/worker views. submit_plan's rails check (util/rails.ts checkPlanRails) is a lowercase substring scan of step text plus files. ToolTestHarness writes raw task JSON (good for seeding legacy/corrupt rows); its project forbids 'rm -rf'. F01 held-out approvalRevision.acceptance.test.ts has no F03 group and must stay unchanged. EOL: schema.ts, taskStore.ts and validators.ts are CRLF; submitPlan.ts, getContext.ts and docs are LF. isEpicFinal shows true only because this row's order (225.5) is the epic's highest; F12 remains the real integration/hardening task, so do not widen scope to whole-epic integration.
planningNotes.risks:
- Own undefined key after a clear: memory and disk differ until reload. Every read uses === undefined; tests assert both getTask() and file bytes.
- A legacy submission must not add the key (Object.keys assertion), or toStrictEqual-style consumers and byte-identical payloads drift.
- WSL test env: Windows node_modules in the shared checkout. Use the Linux snapshot + symlinked Linux node_modules, unset MOE_* (seat env leaks into daemon tests), Linux-only PATH.
- Contested-path landing: peers may declare schema.ts/taskStore.ts/getContext.ts/docs. Edit only with Edit/Write tools and report every path in complete_step.modifiedFiles.
- Rails grep source and plan text: never spell the dunder-proto key or the dynamic-code call token in tests.
- A future board client sending a malformed contract fails its whole UPDATE_TASK (intended fail-closed, same as an invalid priority).
- Docs must describe the landed code exactly; the SCHEMA.md planRevision section is currently stale from F02.
